recruit_text.backstory: Nineteen years of night shifts at a hospice outside Preston taught Graham that a slow ending can be a kind one, if somebody pays attention. Affliction came to him easily, and that bothered him more than anything else here, until he worked out it's the same patience pointed the other way. He's gentle, tired and very good company.

stages.stranger: I'm Graham, love. I'm a warlock now, affliction, and before that I was a nurse, nights mostly. Sit down a minute if you need to. I'll be at the back, and I'll be slow, and slow's the point.
stages.acquaintance: I'm from Blackpool, love. Dad drove the buses and Mum ran a café on the front, and I grew up smelling of chips and sea air. I trained as a nurse at twenty-two and went straight into hospice work outside Preston. Nineteen years of nights, families in corridors, and the long quiet hours when somebody's going. You learn to sit still.
stages.companion: My husband's called Tom. He teaches music at a primary school, and he sings in the car whether you like it or not, very loudly and very badly. We met at a karaoke night. He gave me this watch the year we married. Nurses pin them upside down so you can read them while you take a pulse. The thing I'm frightened of is the magic, pet. Affliction came to me as easy as anything, and I worry what that says about nineteen years at the bedside.
stages.friend: I lost a lot of people at the hospice. That's the job. I remember the ones who were frightened, and I remember the moment each of them stopped being frightened, and that's what I kept going back for. Now there's a traveller at the Pale Watch who says there's a choir at the Bulwark, transplant soldiers, led by an Englishman who sings terribly and makes everyone join in. The road there's all plague country. Will you come with me?
stages.sworn: We heard it from outside the chapel, love, some poor hymn being murdered at full volume, and I knew. Tom stopped in the middle of a verse when he saw me at the back. Then he finished it, because the choir needed him, and walked down the aisle. I couldn't say a word. He said, you took your time, love. We're planting the garden at the Pale Watch now, and he sings to the seedlings. He's given me a new watch, so you have the old one. It kept time while I waited.

moments.prompt: Without seeming to notice, Graham has two fingers on your wrist and he's looking at his watch.

options.reply: Steady as a rock, pet. Sorry, it's habit, nineteen years of it.
Sorry, love, I didn't even know I was doing it. I'll ask first next time.

moments.prompt: On the road to the Bulwark, a patrol is dying slowly of something nobody can treat. Graham wants to stay with them.

options.text: Stay with them. I'll keep watch.
options.reply: Thank you, love. It won't be long, and nobody should be on their own for it.
We can, and we will. Nobody dies alone if I've got any say in it.

lines.bored_warning: We've been at this a while and nobody's needed me, pet. I'd rather be sat with somebody who does.
lines.leaving_good: A good few days, love, and thank you. I'm off to the Pale Watch to make a proper brew and stare at my bit of ground.
lines.leaving_bored: Nowt's happening out here that needs a nurse. I'll be at the Pale Watch.
lines.after_wipe: Right, nobody panic. Breathe slow, look at me, and we'll sort the rest in a minute.
lines.wipe_warning: That's a lot of dying for one day, even by my standards. I'll see this through, but then I want a quiet night or two.
lines.wipe_leave: I'm done in, love, properly. I'll be at the Pale Watch, sleeping it off.
lines.zone_warning: Listen, pet, I've sat with enough people at the end to know what it looks like coming. It looks like this place.
lines.zone_leave: I won't walk you into that, and I won't walk myself into it either. I'll be at the Pale Watch.
lines.gear_refuse: Not just yet, love. Give it a few more trips.
lines.gear_taken: Go on, then. I've worked nights with less.
lines.gear_short: I'm a bit draughty without that piece, love. Just so it's on your list.
lines.gear_upgrade: Ooh, look at that. Thank you, love, that's very thoughtful.
lines.back: Watch is wound, tea's drunk, and I'm ready. Where are we off?
lines.send_word: Graham has sent word from the Pale Watch. He's had his tea and he's ready.
lines.walkout_talk: That was me at the end of a long shift, and you didn't deserve it. Sit with me a minute and I'll tell you what got to me.
lines.neglect: Hello there, stranger. I kept a chair by the fire for you, and a cup, and they both went cold.
lines.asked_to_stay: Go on, I've got another one in me.
lines.on_break: Graham is back at the Pale Watch, sitting with the sick. Come back after you've done a few more jobs.
lines.quest_abandoned: Somebody's still waiting on us for that, love. I don't like leaving folk waiting.

town_arrive.text: My dad drove the buses along the front in Blackpool for twenty years. I still want to wave at anything with wheels.

close_call.text: Slow breaths, pet, in through the nose. There, that's better.

dungeon_clear.text: That was a long one. Let's have a sit and a brew before anyone does owt else.

boss_down.text: It took its time going. I don't hold that against anything.
